actions-list.actionItem: Pursuant to the order of yesterday, the Journal of the proceedings of the Senate was deemed approved to date.
Pursuant to the order of yesterday,the morning hour being deemed expired, and the times for the recognition of the two leaders being reserved.
The following transactions of morning business occurred on today.

H.R. 973 (Rep. Torres):
        A bill to establish consumer standards for lithium-ion batteries.

        -- Passed Senate without amendment by Unanimous Consent.


 H.R. 1520 (Rep. Cammack):
        A bill to prohibit discrimination on the basis of mental or physical disability in cases of organ transplants.

        -- Senate Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions discharged by Unanimous Consent.

        -- Measure laid before Senate by unanimous consent.

        -- Passed Senate with an amendment by Unanimous Consent.
 

 S.Amdt. 7028 (Sen. Moody):
        In the nature of a substitute.

        --Amendment SA 7028 proposed by Senator Moody.

        --Amendment SA 7028 agreed to in Senate by Unanimous Consent.




 H.R. 2347 (Rep. Smucker):
        A bill to amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to exclude from gross income any damages, other than punitive damages, received on account of any sexual acts or sexual contact.

        -- Considered by Senate.

        -- Passed Senate with an amendment by Yea-Nay Vote. 62 - 33. Record Vote Number: 270 



 H.R. 4624 (Rep. Jack):
        A bill to amend the Professional Boxing Safety Actof 1996 to establish requirements for unified boxing organizations, to further enhance the well-being of professional boxers, and for other purposes.

        -- Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation discharged by Unanimous Consent.

        -- Measure laid before Senate by unanimous consent.

        -- Passed Senate with an amendment by Unanimous Consent.
 

 S.Amdt. 7029 (Sen. Cruz):
        In the nature of a substitute.

        --Amendment SA 7029 proposed by Senator Gillibrand for Senator Cruz.

        --Amendment SA 7029 agreed to in Senate by Unanimous Consent.




 H.Con.Res. 93 (Rep. Moulton):
        A concurrent resolution directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran.

        -- Senate Committee on Foreign Relations discharged, under the order of 11/9/26.

        -- Failed of passage in Senate by Yea-Nay Vote. 48 - 51. Record Vote Number: 269 



 S. 580 (Sen. Peters):
        A bill to require the Secretary of Commerce to provide training and guidance relating to violations of human rights, including such abuses perpetrated against Uyghur and other religious and ethnic minority groups by the Government of the People's Republic of China,and for other purposes.

        -- Measure laid before Senate by unanimous consent.

        -- Passed Senate with an amendment and an amendment to the Title by Unanimous Consent.
 

 S.Amdt. 7033 (Sen. Peters):
        In the nature of a substitute.

        --Amendment SA 7033 proposed by Senator Moreno for Senator Peters.

        --Amendment SA 7033 agreed to in Senate by Unanimous Consent.


 S.Amdt. 7034 (Sen. Peters):
        To amend the title.

        --Amendment SA 7034 proposed by Senator Moreno for Senator Peters.

        --Amendment SA 7034 agreed to in Senate by Unanimous Consent.




 S. 1135 (Sen. Curtis):
        A bill to amend the National Trails System Act to direct the Secretary of Agriculture to conduct a study on the feasibility of designating the Bonneville Shoreline Trail.

        -- Passed Senate with an amendment and an amendment to the Title by Unanimous Consent.


 S. 1288 (Sen. Gillibrand):
        A bill to amend the John D. Dingell, Jr. Conservation, Management, and Recreation Act to designate as a component ofthe National Heritage Area System the Finger Lakes National Heritage Area in the State of New York, and for other purposes.

        -- Passed Senate without amendment by Unanimous Consent.


 S. 2479 (Sen. Blackburn):
        A bill to amend the charter of the Reserve Organization of the United States, and for other purposes.

        -- Senate Committee on the Judiciary discharged by Unanimous Consent.

        -- Measure laid before Senate by unanimous consent.

        -- Passed Senate with an amendment by Unanimous Consent.
 

 S.Amdt. 7032 (Sen. Blackburn):
        In the nature of a substitute.

        --Amendment SA 7032 proposed by Senator Moreno for Senator Blackburn.

        --Amendment SA 7032 agreed to in Senate by Unanimous Consent.




 S. 3321 (Sen. Ernst):
        A bill to amend the Family and Medical Leave Act of 1993, to repeal certain limits on leave for married individuals employedby the same employer.

        -- Senate Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions discharged by Unanimous Consent.

        -- Passed Senate without amendment by Voice Vote.


 S. 4035 (Sen. Schiff):
        A bill to amend the Commodity Exchange Act to prohibit the listing of contracts relating to war, death, and similar activities.

        -- Senate Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry discharged by Unanimous Consent.

        -- Measure laid before Senate by unanimous consent.

        -- Passed Senate with an amendment by Voice Vote.
 

 S.Amdt. 7031 (Sen. Schiff):
        To improve the bill.

        --Amendment SA 7031 proposed by Senator Schiff.

        --Amendment SA 7031 agreed to in Senate by Unanimous Consent.




 S. 4238 (Sen. McCormick):
        A bill to amend the John D. Dingell, Jr. Conservation, Management, and Recreation Act to designate as a component ofthe National Heritage Area System the Endless Mountains National Heritage Area in the State of Pennsylvania, and for other purposes.

        -- Passed Senate without amendment by Unanimous Consent.


 S. 4448 (Sen. Thune):
        A bill to require the Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Communications and Information to create tools for tracking the progress of grant recipients under the Broadband Equity, Access, and Deployment Program, to require the Assistant Secretary to help executive agencies improve compliance with the statutory deadline for processing communications use applications, and for other purposes.

        -- Passed Senate with an amendment by Unanimous Consent.


 S. 4538 (Sen. Fetterman):
        A bill to amend the National Trails System Act to direct the Secretary of the Interior to conduct a study on the feasibility of designating Washington's Trail-1753 as a national historic trail, and for other purposes.

        -- Passed Senate without amendment by Unanimous Consent.


 S.Res. 858 (Sen. Klobuchar):
        A resolution honoring the life and legacy of the late Constance Benjamin Clery.

        -- Senate Committee on the Judiciary discharged by Unanimous Consent.

        -- Resolution agreed to in Senate without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent.


 S.Res. 964 (Sen. Cramer):
        A resolution designating November 21, 2026, as National Adoption Day and November 2026 as National Adoption Month to promote national awareness of adoption and the children awaiting families, celebrating children and families involved in adoption, and encouraging thepeople of the United States to secure safety, permanency, and well-being for all children.

        -- Submitted in the Senate, considered, and agreed to without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent.


 S.Res. 965 (Sen. Baldwin):
        A resolution congratulating the Milwaukee Brewers on winning the 2026 Major League Baseball World Series.

        -- Submitted in the Senate, considered, and agreed to without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent.


 S.Res. 966 (Sen. Barrasso):
        A resolution designating November 19, 2026, as "National Rural Health Day".

        -- Submitted in the Senate, considered, and agreed to without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent.

PN1272-4:
        Richard Wesley Bennett, of Texas, to be United States District Judge for the Southern District of Texas

        -- By unanimous consent agreement, mandatory quorum required under Rule XXII waived.

        -- Cloture invoked in Senate by Yea-Nay Vote. 48 - 46. Record Vote Number: 271 


        -- Considered by Senate.

        -- By unanimous consent agreement, debate 11/20/2026.
By unanimous consent, on the request of Mr. Lee, at 11:15p.m., the Senate adjourned, under its order of today, until 10 a.m. tomorrow.
